{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-az-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"e7b62c05d49a464cf401edf98a9afe5b5fdb51190eb4eb5dab8fa06300934f3e","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-az-class-d:lineage:130","source_registry_sha256":"6dbbc2d22fea619728bdb90038a4aedf3afc07eab652b3f97027c9c69aaadaf4","source_liveness_sha256":"1c5753487760cbe2044d84b5696121c7181af61815b598d89d5ce158abf5fe43"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Crash duty, vehicle removal, failure-to-stop and traffic stop confusables","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: moving a vehicle versus leaving the scene, the failure-to-stop ladder, suspension versus revocation, and what to do and not do during a traffic stop","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: moving a vehicle versus leaving the scene, the failure-to-stop ladder, suspension versus revocation, and what to do and not do during a traffic stop
Look-alike duties and penalties from the crash procedure and traffic stop pages, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec22-R01 | anchor: A01
When a crash involves no serious physical injury or death, vehicles must be removed from the main traveled roadway if they remain safely operable under their own power without needing towing and moving them will not cause further vehicle damage or increase traffic hazards [A01].
Why it matters: group vehicle removal; difficulty three; confusable sec22-F09 versus sec22-F10.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec22-R02 | anchor: A01
Moving your car before police arrive is protected, since the move alone cannot make you liable or at fault for the crash. [A01]
Why it matters: group vehicle removal; difficulty two; prereq sec22-F11.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec22-R03 | anchor: A01
A driver in a crash calls the police immediately when someone is injured, while a bystander arriving first calls 911 and warns traffic through others. [A01]
Why it matters: group crash calls; difficulty two; confusable sec22-F03 versus sec22-F06.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec22-R04 | anchor: A02
Moving to the shoulder, median or an exit after a crash is expected, but leaving the crash scene altogether is never allowed. [A02]
Why it matters: group crash duty; difficulty two; confusable sec22-F16 versus sec22-F18.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec22-R05 | anchor: A02
Failing to stop at a damage-only crash brings a 1-year suspension, while failing to stop at a crash with injury brings a 3-year revocation. [A02]
Why it matters: group failure to stop; difficulty three; confusable sec22-F22 versus sec22-F23.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec22-R06 | anchor: A02
Failing to stop at a crash with serious physical injury brings a 5-year revocation, while a crash with a death brings 10 years, and neither counts time spent incarcerated. [A02]
Why it matters: group failure to stop; difficulty three; confusable sec22-F24 versus sec22-F25.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec22-R07 | anchor: A03
You keep your hands visible and wait for instructions before reaching, but you speak up right away if there is a weapon in the vehicle. [A03]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty two; confusable sec22-F37 versus sec22-F36.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec22-R08 | anchor: A03
During a stop you stay in the vehicle unless told to get out, and if told to get out you keep your hands visible and stand where directed. [A03]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty two; confusable sec22-F31 versus sec22-F41.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec22-R09 | anchor: A03
Signing a ticket is not an admission of guilt, while refusing to sign it may lead to arrest. [A03]
Why it matters: group tickets; difficulty two; prereq sec22-F44.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec22-R10 | anchor: A03
A disagreement with an officer is settled later in court, not by arguing during the stop. [A03]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty one; prereq sec22-F43.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec22-R11 | anchor: A03
A complaint about an officer's conduct goes to the officer's agency, where you can ask for a supervisor, ideally soon after the stop [A03] [A04].
Why it matters: group complaints; difficulty one; prereq sec22-F45.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0073]
